gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states, for a 5,000 W kit sold as one listing, the full-sun hours its own panels need to refill it beside its price per Wh: 25.6 / 12.8 / 8.5 h for BLUETTI's 5 kWh RV Kit with 2 / 4 / 6 × 100 W ($0.742 / $0.798 / $0.853 per Wh at the link price) against 4.3 h for Sun Gold Power's 6 × 200 W kit ($0.553 per Wh at the store price).
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts' 240 V solar-input page (cited), StormWatts' kits-at-the-same-panel-watts page and MachineFanatic's 5000W guide. The cited StormWatts page already gives refill hours for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus with 2 × SolarSaga 500 X (about 6.8 h) and station-only $/Wh, but with panels sold separately; it has no kit row. StormWatts' kit page has kit $/Wh and refill figures but stops at 3,763 Wh and says it left 5 kWh kits out. MachineFanatic gives no prices and its Jackery bundle is a 2 × 200 W one. ChatGPT's own answer already carries a generic refill table by panel watts, so the idea is partly there. The other cited page, solargenreview.com, returned HTTP 429 on three tries and was not read, so this score is capped at 1; solargenadvisor.com failed on a certificate error.
decides: Three kits we link clear the 5,000 W line and ship now: the BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit with 2, 4 or 6 × 100 W. Each added pair of panels costs the same $1.50 per W at the store, so the 6 × 100 W kit is the honest pick among them: 8.5 full-sun hours to refill against 25.6 for the 2 × 100 W kit, for $570 more at the link price. Sun Gold Power's SGM-5K5E beats all three on arithmetic (1,200 W of panels, 4.3 h, $0.553 per Wh at $2,831), but it is a wire-it-yourself component kit with a 120 V inverter and has no cart-tested link price in the table. The Jackery 5000 Plus that ChatGPT picked is a pre-order on jackery.com today (station ships Dec 2, 500 X panel by Dec 5), so it cannot be the ships-now pick. The Anker SOLIX S5000 + 2 × 400 W kit is 4,500 W, under the line. No kit's included panels carry more than 24% of a 5,000 W load.
candidates: Jackery Solar Generator 5000 Plus + 2 × SolarSaga 500 X

findings.label: Minutes at a full 5,000 W load on one charge
findings.value: 61 min on nameplate; 52–55 min on BLUETTI's stated usable share
findings.source_title: A Deep Dive into the BLUETTI RV5 48V DIY Solar Inverter Kit
findings.note: 5,120 Wh / 5,000 W × 60 = 61 min. BLUETTI's guide gives the B4810 as 5,120 Wh with about 85–89% usable: 4,352–4,557 Wh / 5,000 W × 60 = 52–55 min. Inverter loss (guide: about 94% efficiency) is not applied. RV5 is 5,000 W continuous, 10,000 W surge per the product page.

findings.label: Share of a 5,000 W load the kit's panels carry at rated output
findings.note: 200 / 5,000, 400 / 5,000, 600 / 5,000. One full-sun hour on 600 W returns 600 Wh, which is 600 / 5,000 × 60 = 7.2 min of 5,000 W running; on 200 W it is 2.4 min.

findings.label: PV input voltage limit
findings.value: 50 V Voc; panels wired in parallel
findings.source_title: A Deep Dive into the BLUETTI RV5 48V DIY Solar Inverter Kit
findings.note: BLUETTI's guide: 'a strict 50V VOC (Voltage Open Circuit) limit on the PV input'. Same guide: the PV2 input doubles as an alternator charger at up to 1,200 W. This is an installed RV system, not a roll-out power station.
